correctness.rationale: The edge evolution follows exactly by subtraction of the weighted nonlinear vertex equations. For a tight edge with \(|e_i|=1\), cyclic closure reduces the remaining feasible gradients to 3-, 4-, 5- and >=6-edge polytopes; their scalar maxima are explicitly evaluated with full boundary regimes and attained. The Dini derivative of a finite maximum gives a sharp global coefficient. The all-weights contraction equivalence follows by scalar comparison and an attaining positive derivative when \(K>0\). Summing long-cycle coefficients and telescoping the conductance increments proves \(c_i\) constant; the pentagon example has a unique monotone \(\ell_r\)-norm transition. An independently executable standard-library checker verified 3600 numerical sharp witnesses, 630 exact rational cubic witnesses, 1712 exact finite-grid inequalities, and parameter diagnostics. No finite experiment is used to justify the universal quantifiers.

The surprising six-vertex rigidity holds irrespective of vertex masses and nonlinear exponent, while the five-cycle has a new sharp subquadratic exponent transition, giving a structural contrast that cannot be read off from vertex ℓq contractions.
